title: What to Do After a Traumatic Event: Advice from a Psychologist

sentences.en: Psychologists, what if you could earn money beyond trading your time for money?
sentences.zh: 心理学家们，如果你们能赚到除了用时间换金钱以外的收入，会怎样？

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, clinical psychologist, and I've been developing passive and recurring income streams since 2019.
sentences.zh: 我是临床心理学家 Marianne Trent 博士，自 2019 年以来，我一直在开发被动和经常性的收入来源。

sentences.en: I have some exciting news.
sentences.zh: 我有一个令人兴奋的消息。

sentences.en: Sophie Foote's One-to-Many program is now open for enrollment.
sentences.zh: Sophie Foote 的“一对多”项目现已开放报名。

sentences.en: It's designed to help you turn your expertise into scalable offers like courses, memberships, and digital products.
sentences.zh: 它旨在帮助你将专业知识转化为可扩展的产品，如课程、会员资格和数字产品。

sentences.en: I completed the program myself in 2022 and have since supported two cohorts of psychologists through their journeys too.
sentences.zh: 我自己于 2022 年完成了该项目，此后也支持了两批心理学家走过他们的旅程。

sentences.en: And if you join through my affiliate link, you'll receive Sophie's bonuses plus my own exclusive support package at no extra coSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你通过我的联盟链接加入，你将获得 Sophie 的奖励，以及我提供的独家支持套餐，无需额外费用。

sentences.en: That includes six months of WhatsApp support, four group masterminds, masterclasses, personalized guidance, a Fortnum and Mason treat, and a time-limited one-to-one coaching bonus.
sentences.zh: 这包括六个月的 WhatsApp 支持、四次小组智囊团会议、大师班、个性化指导、一份 Fortnum and Mason 的礼物，以及限时的一对一辅导奖励。

sentences.en: Enrollment closes on Monday the 16th of November at 10pm.
sentences.zh: 报名将于 11 月 16 日星期一晚上 10 点截止。

sentences.en: Find out more via my bonus page linked in the description.
sentences.zh: 通过描述中链接的我的奖励页面了解更多信息。

sentences.en: And remember, you must purchase through my link to receive my bonuses.
sentences.zh: 请记住，你必须通过我的链接购买才能获得我的奖励。

sentences.en: I'm here if you have any questions.
sentences.zh: 如果你有任何问题，我随时为你解答。

sentences.en: Something awful has happened.
sentences.zh: 发生了一些可怕的事情。

sentences.en: Maybe to you, maybe to someone you care about.
sentences.zh: 也许发生在你身上，也许发生在你关心的人身上。

sentences.en: It might have been a car accident, a mugging, something distressing at work, or witnessing something traumatic in everyday life.
sentences.zh: 可能是车祸、抢劫、工作中令人痛苦的事情，或者在日常生活中目睹了创伤性事件。

sentences.en: Whatever it was you or someone you care about has been left feeling a bit out of sorts.
sentences.zh: 无论是什么，你或你关心的人现在感觉有点不对劲。

sentences.en: Maybe jumpy, wired, tearful, or exhausted.
sentences.zh: 也许感到惊慌、紧张、想哭或精疲力竭。

sentences.en: Or maybe you or they are not feeling much of anything yet, and you are left wondering what's normal after something like this.
sentences.zh: 或者也许你或他们还没有什么特别的感觉，你只是在想，经历这种事后，什么才是正常的。

sentences.en: I am Dr. Marianne Trent, a clinical psychologist, and in this episode we are going to be exploring how people often respond to trauma,
sentences.zh: 我是临床心理学家 Marianne Trent 博士，在这一集中，我们将探讨人们通常如何应对创伤，

sentences.en: what kind of reactions are common, what tends to help, and how to tell when someone might benefit from additional support.
sentences.zh: 什么样的反应是常见的，什么往往有帮助，以及如何判断某人是否可能需要额外的支持。

sentences.en: My hope is that by the end of this episode, you will feel more confident in knowing what's normal, what's to be expected,
sentences.zh: 我希望在本集结束时，你能更有信心地知道什么是正常的，什么是可以预料的，

sentences.en: and what might signal that someone needs a little more help.
sentences.zh: 以及什么可能预示着某人需要更多的帮助。

sentences.en: Hope you find it so useful.
sentences.zh: 希望你觉得这很有用。

sentences.en: Hi, welcome along.
sentences.zh: 嗨，欢迎收听。

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne, and I'm a qualified clinical psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 我是 Marianne 博士，我是一名合格的临床心理学家。

sentences.en: I'm also a specialist in trauma, and often people will get in contact with me to say, this has happened, what do I do?
sentences.zh: 我也是创伤方面的专家，人们经常联系我说：“发生了这种事，我该怎么办？”

sentences.en: This episode is all about that.
sentences.zh: 这一集就是关于这个主题的。

sentences.en: You might be working with people in post-traumatic situations, or you might be someone that just loves or cares about or has experienced something really scary yourself.
sentences.zh: 你可能正在与处于创伤后情况的人一起工作，或者你可能是一个爱着、关心着某人，或者自己经历了一些非常可怕事情的人。

sentences.en: I really hope you find this content helpful.
sentences.zh: 我真心希望你觉得这些内容有帮助。

sentences.en: If you are finding the content helpful, I'd be so grateful if you drop me a like and a comment, and even a subscribe if you're watching on YouTube.
sentences.zh: 如果你觉得这些内容有帮助，如果你能在 YouTube 上点赞、评论甚至订阅，我将不胜感激。

sentences.en: So firstly, when something big or scary happens, it's really normal that because we're human, that we are going to respond to that.
sentences.zh: 首先，当重大或可怕的事情发生时，因为我们是人类，我们会对此做出反应，这是非常正常的。

sentences.en: What we might think of as emotional aftershocks might happen immediately after the event, or might be a bit delayed too.
sentences.zh: 我们可能认为的情绪余震可能会在事件发生后立即出现，也可能会有所延迟。

sentences.en: It can be helpful to group these responses into one of four categories.
sentences.zh: 将这些反应归纳为四类之一可能会有所帮助。

sentences.en: They are physical, emotional, behavioral, and cognitive.
sentences.zh: 它们是生理、情绪、行为和认知。

sentences.en: And what we know is that sometimes people might initially feel fine or say that they're fine, but that doesn't always mean that that's going to stay that way.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，有时人们最初可能感觉还好，或者说他们很好，但这并不总是意味着情况会一直保持那样。

sentences.en: And of course, what we know about people is they may not always tell you the truth.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们对人的了解是，他们并不总是会告诉你真相。

sentences.en: So being able to tune into the person and looking out for these signs and symptoms
sentences.zh: 因此，能够关注对方，留意这些迹象和症状，

sentences.en: might be really useful in helping you to work out whether you or someone you care about really is fine.
sentences.zh: 对于帮助你判断你或你关心的人是否真的还好，可能非常有用。

sentences.en: Let's take a look at the physical symptoms that someone might experience from stress-related or traumatic events.
sentences.zh: 让我们来看看某人因压力相关或创伤性事件可能经历的生理症状。

sentences.en: So they are fatigue, nausea, muscle tremors, twitches, chest pains, difficulty or changes in breathing,
sentences.zh: 它们包括疲劳、恶心、肌肉震颤、抽搐、胸痛、呼吸困难或变化，

sentences.en: increased blood pressure, rapid heart rate, thirst, headaches, visual difficulties or changes,
sentences.zh: 血压升高、心率加快、口渴、头痛、视觉困难或变化，

sentences.en: vomiting, vomiting, vomiting, grinding teeth, weakness, dizziness, profuse sweating, chills, shock, fainting.
sentences.zh: 呕吐、磨牙、虚弱、头晕、大量出汗、发冷、休克、昏厥。

sentences.en: A few of those are flagged for if you experience them or someone you care about experiences them that medical advice should be sought.
sentences.zh: 其中一些症状被标记为：如果你或你关心的人经历这些，应该寻求医疗建议。

sentences.en: And those were the ones like chest pains, difficulty or changes in breathing, a rapid heart rate, headaches, visual difficulties or changes, shock and fainting.
sentences.zh: 这些症状包括胸痛、呼吸困难或变化、心率加快、头痛、视觉困难或变化、休克和昏厥。

sentences.en: The second of our groups of symptoms falls into the thoughts category.
sentences.zh: 我们的第二组症状属于思维类别。

sentences.en: And that might include things like blaming someone, confusion, poor attention, poor decisions,
sentences.zh: 这可能包括责怪他人、困惑、注意力不集中、决策能力差、

sentences.en: heightened or lowered alertness, poor concentration, memory problems, difficulty identifying familiar
sentences.zh: 警觉性过高或过低、专注力差、记忆问题、难以识别熟悉的事物或人、

sentences.en: things or people, poor problem solving, loss of person, place or time orientation, disturbed thinking and nightmares.
sentences.zh: 解决问题能力差、对人、地点或时间失去方向感、思维紊乱和噩梦。

sentences.en: The third of our symptoms are grouped in the emotional category.
sentences.zh: 我们的第三组症状归类在情绪类别中。

sentences.en: And they might include anxiety, guilt, grief, denial, severe panic, which can be rarer, fear, uncertainty,
sentences.zh: 它们可能包括焦虑、内疚、悲伤、否认、严重的恐慌（这可能较少见）、恐惧、不确定性、

sentences.en: loss of emotional control, depression or low mood, feeling overwhelmed, intense anger, irritability,
sentences.zh: 失去情绪控制、抑郁或情绪低落、感到不知所措、强烈的愤怒、易怒、

sentences.en: being extra hypervigilant and flashbacks.
sentences.zh: 过度警觉和闪回。

sentences.en: The fourth and final group of our symptoms are in the behavioural category.
sentences.zh: 我们的第四组也是最后一组症状属于行为类别。

sentences.en: And they might include changes in level of physical activity, change in speech style or pattern,
sentences.zh: 它们可能包括身体活动水平的变化、说话风格或模式的改变、

sentences.en: withdrawal, emotional outbursts, suspiciousness, poor communication, increased alcohol intake, increased drug or medication consumption, inability to rest, antisocial acts,
sentences.zh: 退缩、情绪爆发、多疑、沟通能力差、酒精摄入增加、药物或药物滥用增加、无法休息、反社会行为、

sentences.en: an intensified startle reflex, pacing around, erratic or jerky movements, agitation and apprehension.
sentences.zh: 惊跳反射增强、来回踱步、动作古怪或抽动、烦躁和忧虑。

sentences.en: Now, of course, many of those signs and symptoms kind of do indicate what it is to be human,
sentences.zh: 当然，许多这些迹象和症状确实表明了身为人类的特质，

sentences.en: but you will know what is normal for you or what is normal for the person that you are concerned about.
sentences.zh: 但你会知道什么对你来说是正常的，或者什么对你所关心的人来说是正常的。

sentences.en: And so it's really tuning in to what changes have happened from what we would call a person's normal baseline.
sentences.zh: 所以，真正重要的是要关注与我们所谓的个人正常基准相比发生了什么变化。

sentences.en: So if somebody already consumes alcohol every day and they continue at the same pace, that's not necessarily an indication that they might be struggling.
sentences.zh: 如果某人本来就每天饮酒，并且他们继续保持同样的频率，这并不一定表明他们可能正在挣扎。

sentences.en: Whereas if they very rarely drink or they usually teetotal and after this traumatic or stressful event,
sentences.zh: 然而，如果他们很少喝酒，或者通常滴酒不沾，而在这次创伤性或压力事件之后，

sentences.en: they begin to consume alcohol on a daily basis or that you notice that they seem to suddenly start appearing drunk, that may, of course, indicate there's been a change.
sentences.zh: 他们开始每天饮酒，或者你注意到他们似乎突然开始显得醉醺醺的，这当然可能表明发生了变化。

sentences.en: Similarly, if somebody usually struggles with migraines and they then get migraines at the normal interval for them,
sentences.zh: 同样，如果某人通常受偏头痛困扰，而他们随后在正常的间隔内出现偏头痛，

sentences.en: it doesn't necessarily mean that they're experiencing the traumatic event.
sentences.zh: 这并不一定意味着他们正在经历创伤事件。

sentences.en: I've put together an entirely fictional case study, which might give us a better idea about what kinds of things we might experience and notice and how this plays out in reality.
sentences.zh: 我整理了一个完全虚构的案例研究，这可能让我们更好地了解我们可能会经历和注意到什么样的事情，以及这在现实中是如何表现的。

sentences.en: As I said, this is entirely a fictional account and not based on anyone that I know or have worked with.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，这是一个完全虚构的叙述，并不基于我认识或共事过的任何人。

sentences.en: Jordan is a 32-year-old marketing manager and they were involved in a multi-car collision on a motorway.
sentences.zh: Jordan 是一位 32 岁的营销经理，他们卷入了一起高速公路上的多车连环相撞事故。

sentences.en: Although they weren't physically injured, they witnessed someone being taken away in an ambulance and were badly shaken by the experience.
sentences.zh: 虽然他们没有身体受伤，但他们目睹了有人被救护车带走，并被这次经历吓坏了。

sentences.en: In the days following the incident, Jordan noticed themselves being unusually tearful, often crying without a clear reason, especially when recalling parts of the event.
sentences.zh: 在事件发生后的几天里，Jordan 注意到自己异常爱哭，经常在没有明确原因的情况下哭泣，尤其是在回想起事件的部分内容时。

sentences.en: Normally quite sociable, they started avoiding phone calls and skipping social plans, preferring to stay at home alone.
sentences.zh: 通常很善于交际的他们开始回避电话并推掉社交计划，宁愿独自呆在家里。

sentences.en: Jordan also found it difficult to fall asleep and was waking up several times during the night, sometimes feeling panicked or sweaty.
sentences.zh: Jordan 还发现很难入睡，并且在夜间多次醒来，有时感到恐慌或出汗。

sentences.en: Loud noises, especially car horns or sirens, started making them jumpy and tense and they began scanning the road obsessively when driving again.
sentences.zh: 巨大的噪音，尤其是汽车喇叭或警笛声，开始让他们感到惊慌和紧张，他们再次开车时开始强迫性地扫描道路。

sentences.en: To try and cope with the tension and the poor sleep,
sentences.zh: 为了试图应对紧张和睡眠不足，

sentences.en: Jordan started drinking more alcohol in the evenings than usual, telling themselves it was just to take the edge off.
sentences.zh: Jordan 开始在晚上比平时喝更多的酒，告诉自己这只是为了缓解压力。

sentences.en: In our case study, we are looking a little further ahead with Jordan, whereas of course you might find that the event has happened right now,
sentences.zh: 在我们的案例研究中，我们对 Jordan 的情况看得更远了一些，当然你可能会发现事件刚刚发生，

sentences.en: but these are useful things to look out for.
sentences.zh: 但这些都是值得注意的事情。

sentences.en: So for example, when Jordan went back to work, they were functioning relatively okay, but found that they felt distracted and exhausted
sentences.zh: 例如，当 Jordan 回到工作岗位时，他们表现得还可以，但发现自己感到分心和精疲力竭，

sentences.en: and had started to wonder whether what they were feeling was normal and whether they should seek help.
sentences.zh: 并开始怀疑自己的感受是否正常，以及是否应该寻求帮助。

sentences.en: So whilst this is not based on an individual known to me, these are a really common collection of signs and symptoms post-trauma.
sentences.zh: 所以，虽然这不是基于我认识的个人，但这些是创伤后非常常见的一系列迹象和症状。

sentences.en: We'll often see people who perhaps have experienced the birth of a child or in birthing their own child will experience some post-trauma.
sentences.zh: 我们经常看到那些可能经历了孩子出生，或者在生下自己的孩子时经历了一些创伤的人。

sentences.en: It is so, so common, but it's often not flagged as being a trauma response.
sentences.zh: 这非常非常普遍，但通常不会被标记为创伤反应。

sentences.en: So these are really important signs and symptoms to look out for.
sentences.zh: 所以这些是非常重要的迹象和症状，需要留意。

sentences.en: So what are the helpful things to be able to do after a traumatic event?
sentences.zh: 那么，在创伤事件发生后，有哪些有益的事情可以做呢？

sentences.en: Firstly, spending time with people that you feel and trust or being around trusted people.
sentences.zh: 首先，与你信任的人共度时光，或者与值得信赖的人在一起。

sentences.en: That might be family, it might be friends, it might be loved ones.
sentences.zh: 这可能是家人，可能是朋友，也可能是爱人。

sentences.en: There can also be some value in spending time with people who are also involved in that experience to help to debrief it a bit too.
sentences.zh: 与也参与了那次经历的人共度时光也有一定的价值，有助于对事件进行一些复盘。

sentences.en: Where possible, maintaining your usual routines can actually be protective of your mental health and functioning.
sentences.zh: 在可能的情况下，保持你平时的作息实际上可以保护你的心理健康和功能。

sentences.en: That it might involve when you get up, when you go to bed, when you rest, when you exercise, when you eat.
sentences.zh: 这可能涉及你什么时候起床、什么时候睡觉、什么时候休息、什么时候锻炼、什么时候吃饭。

sentences.en: If you don't usually exercise, gentle movement or being outside or taking part in physical activity can also be really, really important.
sentences.zh: 如果你平时不锻炼，温和的运动、待在户外或参加体育活动也可以非常非常重要。

sentences.en: Of course, if you've been physically injured as a result of the traumatic incident, that might be problematic.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果你因创伤事件而身体受伤，那可能会有问题。

sentences.en: And so if you have, please do get yourself signed off by your medical practitioner before attempting any physical activity.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你受伤了，请务必在尝试任何体育活动之前先获得医生的许可。

sentences.en: So limiting alcohol and certainly not drinking more than you usually would is absolutely advised.
sentences.zh: 因此，绝对建议限制饮酒，当然不要喝得比平时多。

sentences.en: As well as talking to someone, either a mental health professional or a friend or family about your experiences can be so protective of mental health.
sentences.zh: 此外，与心理健康专业人士或朋友或家人谈论你的经历，对心理健康非常有保护作用。

sentences.en: Only taking medication as prescribed and not being swayed by any unprescribed or recreational drugs can be so important.
sentences.zh: 只按处方服用药物，不被任何非处方药或娱乐性药物所左右，这非常重要。

sentences.en: If you find that your symptoms are not being managed by what you're already prescribed, please do contact your prescribing clinician as soon as possible.
sentences.zh: 如果你发现你的症状无法通过你已经服用的药物来控制，请尽快联系你的开方医生。

sentences.en: Knowing that the way that our brains work is that we will process things.
sentences.zh: 要知道我们大脑的工作方式是我们会处理事情。

sentences.en: It might feel like we're feeling really intense reactions right now, but knowing that these are likely to pass and we won't always feel this way can be so powerful too.
sentences.zh: 现在感觉反应非常强烈，但知道这些很可能会过去，我们不会一直有这种感觉，这也会非常有力量。

sentences.en: Let's talk about some of the things that I recommend to people post-trauma, which can be really helpful.
sentences.zh: 让我们谈谈我推荐给创伤后人们的一些事情，这些事情真的很有帮助。

sentences.en: Firstly is our before, during and after approach.
sentences.zh: 首先是我们的“之前、期间和之后”方法。

sentences.en: This is where we split the chunks of time around the incident into three.
sentences.zh: 这是我们将事件前后的时间段分成三部分的方法。

sentences.en: So the before section would be maybe from when you first woke up that day and everything was normal, all the things you did or they did,
sentences.zh: 所以“之前”部分可能是从你那天早上刚醒来，一切都很正常，你或他们所做的所有事情开始，

sentences.en: which ran up until the time when just before you noticed something was different.
sentences.zh: 一直持续到你注意到事情有所不同之前的那一刻。

sentences.en: So for example, in the case of Jordan, they got up that day, got showered, got breakfasted, dropped children off at school,
sentences.zh: 例如，在 Jordan 的案例中，他们那天起床、洗澡、吃早餐、送孩子上学，

sentences.en: then got in the car and listened to the radio and was driving.
sentences.zh: 然后上车听广播开车。

sentences.en: Perhaps you tune in to the memory of the songs or the stories that were being discussed.
sentences.zh: 也许你调到了歌曲或正在讨论的故事的记忆中。

sentences.en: And then even before, the first thing that happened, and that is the before section.
sentences.zh: 甚至在第一件事发生之前，这就是“之前”部分。

sentences.en: The during section starts as soon as you begin to notice that something is not normal.
sentences.zh: “期间”部分从你开始注意到事情不正常的那一刻开始。

sentences.en: So again, with Jordan's example, it might be suddenly seeing a stopped queue of traffic in front of them and then needing to put your brakes on.
sentences.zh: 同样，以 Jordan 的例子为例，这可能是突然看到前面停着的车流，然后需要踩刹车。

sentences.en: So that is the during, the during section runs up until you're kind of out the other side, really.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是“期间”，期间部分一直持续到你真正走出来为止。

sentences.en: So that might be when you get home again, perhaps after being checked out by hospital, or it might be when you get dropped off by the car recovery firm, for example.
sentences.zh: 这可能是当你再次回到家时，也许是在医院检查之后，或者可能是当你被汽车救援公司送回家时，例如。

sentences.en: But it's when that kind of section of action is over.
sentences.zh: 但这是当那种行动部分结束的时候。

sentences.en: And that's when the during section spans.
sentences.zh: 这就是“期间”部分所跨越的时间。

sentences.en: I guess one interesting point about the during section is that sometimes when we're assessing people
sentences.zh: 我想关于“期间”部分的一个有趣点是，有时当我们评估人们时，

sentences.en: in clinic is that people really begin to make it clear in the way that they're talking about things
sentences.zh: 在诊所里，人们在谈论事情的方式，

sentences.en: or the way that they are describing what happened is that they still think it's happening now.
sentences.zh: 或者他们描述发生的事情的方式，确实开始变得很清楚，他们仍然认为这正在发生。

sentences.en: They haven't got that sense of safety, which has kind of triggered to them that it's not now that they're safe, that this has passed.
sentences.zh: 他们没有那种安全感，这触发了他们认为现在不是安全的，这已经过去了。

sentences.en: So that is an interesting one to look out for as well.
sentences.zh: 所以这也是一个值得注意的有趣点。

sentences.en: The after section would be, you know, anything after.
sentences.zh: “之后”部分就是，你知道，之后的任何事情。

sentences.en: So anything from once that person is home again until right in this present day.
sentences.zh: 所以从那个人再次回到家直到现在的任何事情。

sentences.en: And you can recount this in as much or little detail as you want.
sentences.zh: 你可以根据需要以尽可能多或尽可能少的细节来讲述这一点。

sentences.en: The theory behind this is that when something traumatic happens, our brains don't always realise that it's not now.
sentences.zh: 这背后的理论是，当创伤性事情发生时，我们的大脑并不总是意识到它不是现在。

sentences.en: This has had a beginning section, a during section and an after section.
sentences.zh: 这有一个开始部分、一个期间部分和一个之后部分。

sentences.en: So helping to really get that flow going can help the sequential processing and help make the body and the mind realise that this is over.
sentences.zh: 所以帮助真正让那个流程进行下去，可以帮助顺序处理，并帮助身体和大脑意识到这已经结束了。

sentences.en: This is not now.
sentences.zh: 这不是现在。

sentences.en: What happens before we do the before, the during and after is that you might struggle to get a coherent order.
sentences.zh: 在我们做“之前、期间和之后”之前发生的事情是，你可能难以获得连贯的顺序。

sentences.en: All of the different bits and pieces about the car crash, for example, in Jordan's example, might feel like you kind of go from A to D to B to Z to T to R to Q.
sentences.zh: 关于车祸的所有不同部分，例如在 Jordan 的例子中，可能感觉就像你从 A 到 D 到 B 到 Z 到 T 到 R 到 Q。

sentences.en: And doing this sequential before, during and after can really help the body and the mind to process and assimilate and make sense of the order that this happened in.
sentences.zh: 做这个顺序的“之前、期间和之后”真的可以帮助身体和大脑处理、吸收并理解这发生的顺序。

sentences.en: What can be also really nice, especially if you're working with a child, is to get them to draw their before, their during and their after.
sentences.zh: 同样非常好的事情，特别是如果你和孩子一起工作，是让他们画出他们的“之前”、“期间”和“之后”。

sentences.en: Try not to judge or criticise.
sentences.zh: 尽量不要评判或批评。

sentences.en: Just be open to conversations about what it is that the person has drawn.
sentences.zh: 只要对关于那个人画了什么的对话保持开放态度。

sentences.en: And that's regardless of age.
sentences.zh: 而且这与年龄无关。

sentences.en: It's not just children that draw.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是孩子画画。

sentences.en: Sometimes being able to tap into different ways of doing, as well as the spoken word, can really help the body and the mind to process all of this.
sentences.zh: 有时能够利用不同的做事方式，以及口头语言，真的可以帮助身体和大脑处理所有这些。

sentences.en: Similarly, you might find it helpful to write your experiences in terms of before, during and after too.
sentences.zh: 同样，你可能会发现用“之前、期间和之后”来写下你的经历也很有帮助。

sentences.en: If you're finding it very distressing to do this before, during and after section, it's okay to pop it away and come back to it when you feel stronger
sentences.zh: 如果你发现做这个“之前、期间和之后”部分非常痛苦，把它放一边，等你感觉更强壮时再回来，

sentences.en: or to go through it with somebody that you trust or maybe even with a mental health professional too.
sentences.zh: 或者与你信任的人，甚至与心理健康专业人士一起经历它，也是可以的。

sentences.en: When might be an indication that you or someone you care about might need to seek additional help.
sentences.zh: 什么时候可能预示着你或你关心的人可能需要寻求额外的帮助。

sentences.en: So signs that this might not be settling might be prolonged anxiety or worsening anxiety, nightmares, flashbacks, intrusive thoughts and hypervigilance.
sentences.zh: 所以迹象表明这可能没有平息，可能是长期的焦虑或恶化的焦虑、噩梦、闪回、侵入性想法和过度警觉。

sentences.en: It might be a sign that someone's functioning has been severely impacted on.
sentences.zh: 这可能是某人的功能受到严重影响的迹象。

sentences.en: All the things that they would usually do, such as dropping children at school, going to work,
sentences.zh: 他们通常会做的所有事情，例如送孩子上学、去工作、

sentences.en: kind of doing all the different jobs in their family have stopped or changed in some way.
sentences.zh: 在家庭中做所有不同的工作，都已经停止或以某种方式改变了。

sentences.en: And that can be a real indication that all is not well.
sentences.zh: 这可能是一个真正的迹象，表明一切都不好。

sentences.en: If this affects their work, their sleep, their relationships, this is an indication that additional help might be required.
sentences.zh: 如果这影响了他们的工作、睡眠、人际关系，这就是可能需要额外帮助的迹象。

sentences.en: It's really important to reassure people that seeking help is not a sign of weakness.
sentences.zh: 向人们保证寻求帮助不是软弱的迹象，这非常重要。

sentences.en: This is just the way our tricky human brains work and that it's entirely normal.
sentences.zh: 这只是我们棘手的人类大脑工作的方式，这是完全正常的。

sentences.en: Getting help as early as possible is likely to give you a really great chance of recovery.
sentences.zh: 尽早获得帮助很可能会给你一个非常好的康复机会。

sentences.en: Technically speaking, we are allowed to respond to tricky, challenging, stressful events
sentences.zh: 从技术上讲，我们被允许对棘手、具有挑战性、压力大的事件做出反应，

sentences.en: without this necessarily meaning this results in a post-traumatic stress disorder presentation.
sentences.zh: 而不一定意味着这会导致创伤后应激障碍的表现。

sentences.en: You have this with grief as well.
sentences.zh: 你在悲伤时也有这种情况。

sentences.en: It's only really after a couple of months of prolonged experiences of these signs and symptoms that we might begin to think this is cropping up outside of normal limits
sentences.zh: 只有在这些迹象和症状持续几个月后，我们才可能开始认为这超出了正常范围。

sentences.en: and that this is becoming complex, complicated grief or PTSD.
sentences.zh: 这正在演变成复杂的、纠结的悲伤或创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）。

sentences.en: Basically, if you're concerned about anyone, about the risk to themselves or others, please do make contact with mental health services and or police services too, if required.
sentences.zh: 基本上，如果您担心任何人，担心他们对自己或他人构成风险，请务必联系心理健康服务机构，必要时也请联系警方。

sentences.en: If this is something that's happened as a result of a crime, it's also important to get this reported and victim support might well be able to support you too.
sentences.zh: 如果这是犯罪导致的结果，那么报案也很重要，受害者援助机构很可能也能为您提供支持。

sentences.en: There are, of course, specific mental health treatments and approaches such as cognitive behavioural therapy, such as EMDR, such as compassion focused therapy,
sentences.zh: 当然，也有一些特定的心理健康治疗方法和途径，例如认知行为疗法、眼动脱敏再加工疗法（EMDR）、同情心聚焦疗法等，

sentences.en: which really can make a very big difference for how people are feeling and getting this traumatic event to lay flat and to be better assimilated into their life.
sentences.zh: 这些方法确实能对人们的感受产生巨大的影响，让创伤事件变得平复，并更好地融入他们的生活中。

sentences.en: So last but not least, trauma reactions are all part of being human.
sentences.zh: 最后但同样重要的是，创伤反应是身为人类的一部分。

sentences.en: Often when I've been through the tricky brain kit exercise with people, they absolutely then understand the theory, but do wish perhaps there are real benefits to being human,
sentences.zh: 通常当我与人们一起完成“棘手大脑工具包”练习时，他们完全理解了其中的理论，但确实希望身为人类能有一些真正的好处，

sentences.en: one of which being that you can get £10 off the price of a tricky brain kit by using the code YouTube10 at checkout.
sentences.zh: 其中之一就是您在结账时使用代码 YouTube10，购买“棘手大脑工具包”即可享受 10 英镑的优惠。

sentences.en: Hope is so important.
sentences.zh: 希望非常重要。

sentences.en: Recovery is possible.
sentences.zh: 康复是有可能的。

sentences.en: Help is available.
sentences.zh: 寻求帮助的渠道是有的。

sentences.en: If you have been through something traumatic or challenging or someone you care about has, this can feel really derailing.
sentences.zh: 如果您经历过创伤或挑战，或者您关心的人经历过，这可能会让人感觉生活脱轨。

sentences.en: And so my heart goes out to you.
sentences.zh: 所以我对您深表同情。

sentences.en: Please do look after yourselves.
sentences.zh: 请务必照顾好自己。

sentences.en: Please do try and reSt.
sentences.zh: 请务必尝试休息。

sentences.en: Please do try to talk about your experiences.
sentences.zh: 请务必尝试谈论您的经历。

sentences.en: I would love it if you found this helpful.
sentences.zh: 如果您觉得这有帮助，我会很高兴。

sentences.en: If you would like it, if you would drop me a comment, if you would share with others too.
sentences.zh: 如果您愿意的话，请给我留言，也请分享给其他人。

sentences.en: Perhaps if you've been through something traumatic and come out the other side, it might be really helpful and empowering.
sentences.zh: 也许如果您经历过创伤并走出了阴影，这可能会非常有帮助且赋予人力量。

sentences.en: If you were able to drop a comment on YouTube to let others know that this is possible.
sentences.zh: 如果您能在 YouTube 上留言，让其他人知道这是可能的，那就太好了。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for watching or listening to this episode.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您观看或收听本期节目。

sentences.en: I will be along with the next episode from 10am on Saturdays on YouTube and wherever you get your podcast from 6am on Mondays.
sentences.zh: 下一期节目将于周六上午 10 点在 YouTube 上线，并于周一上午 6 点在各大播客平台发布。

sentences.en: Please do take care of yourself and I'll see you very soon.
sentences.zh: 请务必照顾好自己，我们很快再见。

sentences.en: Psychologists, what if you could earn money beyond trading your time for money?
sentences.zh: 心理学家们，如果你们能赚到钱，而不仅仅是用时间换金钱，会怎样？

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, clinical psychologist, and I've been developing passive and recurring income streams since 2019.
sentences.zh: 我是临床心理学家玛丽安·特伦特博士，自 2019 年以来，我一直在开发被动和经常性收入流。

sentences.en: I have some exciting news.
sentences.zh: 我有一个激动人心的消息。

sentences.en: Sophie Foote's One to Many program is now open for enrollment.
sentences.zh: 苏菲·富特的“一对多”项目现已开放报名。

sentences.en: It's designed to help you turn your expertise into scalable offers like courses, memberships, and digital products.
sentences.zh: 它旨在帮助您将专业知识转化为可扩展的产品，如课程、会员资格和数字产品。

sentences.en: I completed the program myself in 2022 and have since supported two cohorts of psychologists through their journeys too.
sentences.zh: 我自己于 2022 年完成了该项目，此后也支持了两批心理学家走过他们的旅程。

sentences.en: And if you join through my affiliate link, you'll receive Sophie's bonuses, plus my own exclusive support package at no extra coSt.
sentences.zh: 如果您通过我的联盟链接加入，您将获得苏菲的奖励，以及我独家提供的额外支持套餐，无需额外费用。

sentences.en: That includes six months of WhatsApp support, four group masterminds, masterclasses, personalized guidance, a Fortnum and Mason treat, and a time-limited one-to-one coaching bonus.
sentences.zh: 其中包括六个月的 WhatsApp 支持、四次小组智囊团会议、大师班、个性化指导、一份福特纳姆和梅森百货的礼品，以及限时的一对一辅导奖励。

sentences.en: Enrollment closes on Monday the 16th of November at 10pm.
sentences.zh: 报名将于 11 月 16 日星期一晚上 10 点截止。

sentences.en: Find out more via my bonus page linked in the description.
sentences.zh: 通过描述中链接的我的奖励页面了解更多信息。

sentences.en: And remember, you must purchase through my link to receive my bonuses.
sentences.zh: 请记住，您必须通过我的链接购买才能获得我的奖励。

sentences.en: I'm here if you have any questions.
sentences.zh: 如果您有任何问题，我都在这里。

sentences.en: You're welcome.
sentences.zh: 不客气。

sentences.en: And remember, you're welcome.
sentences.zh: 请记住，不客气。

sentences.en: We'll see you next time.
sentences.zh: 我们下次见。

sentences.en: Bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。
